card.fund: Nordea 1 – Global Climate and Environment Fund

rules.summary: US persons may not subscribe unless the board or management company decides otherwise; shares may not be offered or sold in the USA. The definition is mixed: a list of criteria that includes 'any other U.S. person defined by US Rule 902 of Regulation S', with a carve-out for 'Non-United States persons' under CFTC Rule 4.7. US taxpayers (and so US citizens) may subscribe as long as they are not US persons, so US citizenship alone does not exclude.

citations.quote: The shares in the SICAV may not be directly or indirectly offered or sold in the USA. Unless otherwise decided by the board or the management company, US persons may not subscribe for shares in the SICAV.
Therefore, US taxpayers, as defined for US federal income tax purposes, may subscribe for shares in the SICAV as long as they do not qualify as US persons.
any other U.S. person defined by US Rule 902 of Regulation S

rules.summary: Shares may be offered or bought only where they are registered for public sale or where local law does not prohibit the sale. The client's jurisdiction must be checked against the class's registration countries (see nordea.lu).

citations.quote: Distributing this prospectus, offering these shares for sale, or investing in these shares is legal only where the shares are registered for public sale or where sale is not prohibited by local law or regulation.
Also, some funds or share classes that are available in certain jurisdictions may not be available in others.

rules.summary: The SICAV may reject any subscription in whole or in part, and may soft-close or hard-close a fund or share class without notice. A dealing desk should treat this as a discretionary block, not a client-eligibility criterion.

citations.quote: Reject or cancel any application to open an account or any request to subscribe for or transfer shares We can reject the entire amount or part of it.
A closure may apply only to new investors (soft closure) or to further investments from existing shareholders as well (hard closure).

rules.summary: BP-EUR is core class P with the accumulating 'B' prefix. Class P is available to all investors, with no management company requirements.

citations.quote: P All investors. Yes None None
For all other classes, shares that DO contain the prefix "B" are accumulation shares.

rules.summary: Prospectus: BI-EUR is core class I, available only to institutional investors. These are defined as investors within the meaning of article 174 of the 2010 Law, such as credit institutions and other financial professionals investing for themselves or for others (including retail clients under a discretionary management agreement), insurance companies, pension funds and other UCIs. This contradicts the BI-EUR KID, which says the fund is suitable for all types of investors.

citations.quote: I Institutional investors. Yes None

institutional investors Investors within the meaning of article 174 of the 2010 Law, such as credit institutions and other financial professionals investing on the behalf of themselves or other investors (whether retail in connection with a discretionary management agreement or institutional), as well as insurance companies, pension funds, or other UCIs.
The fund is suitable for all types of investors through all distribution channels.

rules.summary: BI-EUR KID: 'The fund is suitable for all types of investors through all distribution channels.' This contradicts the prospectus, which reserves core class I to institutional investors. A validator must decide which applies.

citations.quote: The fund is suitable for all types of investors through all distribution channels.
I Institutional investors. Yes None

rules.summary: Class I has a minimum initial investment of EUR 75,000 or the equivalent in other currencies. The minimum applies per share class and per fund, and includes switches. The SICAV may reduce or waive the minimum, consistent with equal treatment of shareholders.

citations.quote: EUR 75,000 or equivalent in other currencies
* Amounts apply for each share class of each fund, and include initial investments made by switches
Reduce or waive any stated sales charge, or minimum initial investment amount, for any share class, fund, investor, or request, so long as it is consistent with equal treatment of shareholders.

rules.summary: Class P is open to all investors, with no written agreement and no requirement for advice or a mandate. It is not reserved to discretionary mandates.

rules.summary: Class I is not formally a mandate-only class: it is open to institutional investors in general. Under the institutional-investor definition, however, retail clients can reach it only through a financial professional acting under a discretionary management agreement.
